verses.text: How the gold has become tarnished, the pure gold has become dull! The gems of the temple lie scattered on every street corner.

xrefs.text: They will throw their silver into the streets, and their gold will seem unclean. Their silver and gold cannot save them in the day of the wrath of the LORD. They cannot satisfy their appetites or fill their stomachs with wealth, for it became the stumbling block that brought their iniquity.

Arise, cry out in the night from the first watch of the night. Pour out your heart like water in the presence of the Lord. Lift up your hands to Him for the lives of your children who are fainting from hunger on the corner of every street.
See how the faithful city has become a harlot! She once was full of justice; righteousness resided within her, but now only murderers!
He burned down the house of the LORD, the royal palace, and all the houses of Jerusalem— every significant building.
“Do you see all these things? He replied. “Truly I tell you, not one stone here will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.

verses.text: How the precious sons of Zion, once worth their weight in pure gold, are now esteemed as jars of clay, the work of a potter’s hands!

xrefs.text: It will break in pieces like a potter’s jar, shattered so that no fragment can be found. Not a shard will be found in the dust large enough to scoop the coals from a hearth or to skim the water from a cistern.”
Does not the potter have the right to make from the same lump of clay one vessel for special occasions and another for common use?

and you are to proclaim to them that this is what the LORD of Hosts says: I will shatter this nation and this city, like one shatters a potter’s jar that can never again be repaired. They will bury the dead in Topheth until there is no more room to bury them.
A large house contains not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and clay. Some indeed are for honorable use, but others are for common use.
Now we have this treasure in jars of clay to show that this surpassingly great power is from God and not from us.

verses.text: Even jackals offer their breasts to nurse their young, but the daughter of my people has become cruel, like an ostrich in the wilderness.

xrefs.text: But Jesus turned to them and said, “Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for Me, but weep for yourselves and for your children.
As a result, fathers among you will eat their sons, and sons will eat their fathers. I will execute judgments against you and scatter all your remnant to every wind.’
Look, O LORD, and consider: Whom have You ever treated like this? Should women eat their offspring, the infants they have nurtured? Should priests and prophets be killed in the sanctuary of the Lord?
The hands of compassionate women have cooked their own children, who became their food in the destruction of the daughter of my people.
The wings of the ostrich flap joyfully, but cannot match the pinions and feathers of the stork.

verses.text: The nursing infant’s tongue clings in thirst to the roof of his mouth. Little children beg for bread, but no one gives them any.

xrefs.text: My strength is dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue sticks to the roof of my mouth. You lay me in the dust of death.
My eyes fail from weeping; I am churning within. My heart is poured out in grief over the destruction of the daughter of my people, because children and infants faint in the streets of the city.
May my tongue cling to the roof of my mouth if I do not remember you, if I do not exalt Jerusalem as my greatest joy!
All her people groan as they search for bread. They have traded their treasures for food to keep themselves alive. Look, O LORD, and consider, for I have become despised.
Which of you, if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone?

verses.text: Those who once ate delicacies are destitute in the streets; those brought up in crimson huddle in ash heaps.

When it snows, she has no fear for her household, for they are all clothed in scarlet.
O daughters of Israel, weep for Saul, who clothed you in scarlet and luxury, who decked your garments with ornaments of gold.

verses.text: The punishment of the daughter of my people is greater than that of Sodom, which was overthrown in an instant without a hand turned to help her.

xrefs.text: Thus He destroyed these cities and the entire plain, including all the inhabitants of the cities and everything that grew on the ground.
Unless the LORD of Hosts had left us a few survivors, we would have become like Sodom, we would have resembled Gomorrah.
For at that time there will be great tribulation, unseen from the beginning of the world until now, and never to be seen again.
I tell you, it will be more bearable on that day for Sodom than for that town.
That servant who knows his master’s will but does not get ready or follow his instructions will be beaten with many blows.

verses.text: Her dignitaries were brighter than snow, whiter than milk; their bodies were more ruddy than rubies, their appearance like sapphires.

xrefs.text: Purify me with hyssop, and I will be clean; wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.
My beloved is dazzling and ruddy, outstanding among ten thousand.
Then our sons will be like plants nurtured in their youth, our daughters like corner pillars carved to adorn a palace.
So Jesse sent for his youngest son and brought him in. He was ruddy, with beautiful eyes and a handsome appearance. And the LORD said, “Rise and anoint him, for he is the one.”
And at the end of ten days, they looked healthier and better nourished than all the young men who were eating the king’s food.

verses.text: But now their appearance is blacker than soot; they are not recognized in the streets. Their skin has shriveled on their bones; it has become as dry as a stick.

xrefs.text: Our skin is as hot as an oven with fever from our hunger.
My skin grows black and peels, and my bones burn with fever.
For my days vanish like smoke, and my bones burn like glowing embers.
My skin and flesh cling to my bones; I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.
Though I am like a wineskin dried up by smoke, I do not forget Your statutes.

verses.text: Those slain by the sword are better off than those who die of hunger, who waste away, pierced with pain because the fields lack produce.

xrefs.text: “They will die from deadly diseases. They will not be mourned or buried, but will lie like dung on the ground. They will be finished off by sword and famine, and their corpses will become food for the birds of the air and beasts of the earth.”
Those of you who survive in the lands of your enemies will waste away in their iniquity and will decay in the sins of their fathers.
Your turbans will remain on your heads and your sandals on your feet. You will not mourn or weep, but you will waste away because of your sins, and you will groan among yourselves.
Now as for you, son of man, tell the house of Israel that this is what they have said: ‘Our transgressions and our sins are heavy upon us, and we are wasting away because of them! How can we live?’

verses.text: The hands of compassionate women have cooked their own children, who became their food in the destruction of the daughter of my people.

“Can a woman forget her nursing child, or lack compassion for the son of her womb? Even if she could forget, I will not forget you!
As the king of Israel was passing by on the wall, a woman cried out to him, “Help me, my lord the king!”
I will make them eat the flesh of their sons and daughters, and they will eat one another’s flesh in the siege and distress inflicted on them by their enemies who seek their lives.’
Streams of tears flow from my eyes over the destruction of the daughter of my people.

verses.text: The LORD has exhausted His wrath; He has poured out His fierce anger; He has kindled a fire in Zion, and it has consumed her foundations.

xrefs.text: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Behold, My anger and My fury will be poured out on this place, on man and beast, on the trees of the field and the produce of the land, and it will burn and not be extinguished.
So I have poured out My indignation upon them and consumed them with the fire of My fury. I have brought their ways down upon their own heads, declares the Lord GOD.”

The LORD has done what He planned; He has accomplished His decree, which He ordained in days of old; He has overthrown you without pity. He has let the enemy gloat over you and exalted the horn of your foes.

But if you do not listen to Me to keep the Sabbath day holy by not carrying a load while entering the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, then I will kindle an unquenchable fire in its gates to consume the citadels of Jerusalem.’”
O Daughter of Zion, your punishment is complete; He will not prolong your exile. But He will punish your iniquity, O Daughter of Edom; He will expose your sins.

verses.text: The kings of the earth did not believe, nor any people of the world, that an enemy or a foe could enter the gates of Jerusalem.

xrefs.text: So all the nations will ask, ‘Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land? Why this great outburst of anger?’
For behold, the kings assembled; they all advanced together.
Behold, I am against you who dwell above the valley, atop the rocky plateau— declares the LORD— you who say, “Who can come against us? Who can enter our dwellings?”
And when this temple has become a heap of rubble, all who pass by it will be appalled and will hiss and say, ‘Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this temple?’

verses.text: But this was for the sins of her prophets and the guilt of her priests, who shed the blood of the righteous in her midst.

xrefs.text: The prophets prophesy falsely, and the priests rule by their own authority. My people love it so, but what will you do in the end?
“For from the least of them to the greatest, all are greedy for gain; from prophet to priest, all practice deceit.
The visions of your prophets were empty and deceptive; they did not expose your guilt to ward off your captivity. The burdens they envisioned for you were empty and misleading.

Her priests do violence to My law and profane My holy things. They make no distinction between the holy and the common, and they fail to distinguish between the clean and the unclean. They disregard My Sabbaths, so that I am profaned among them.
and as soon as he had finished telling all the people everything the LORD had commanded him to say, the priests and prophets and all the people seized him, shouting, “You must surely die!

verses.text: They wandered blind in the streets, defiled by this blood, so that no one dared to touch their garments.

When you spread out your hands in prayer, I will hide My eyes from you; even though you multiply your prayers, I will not listen. Your hands are covered with blood.
Israel’s watchmen are blind, they are all oblivious; they are all mute dogs, they cannot bark; they are dreamers lying around, loving to slumber.
The LORD will afflict you with madness, blindness, and confusion of mind,
Anyone in the open field who touches someone who has been killed by the sword or has died of natural causes, or anyone who touches a human bone or a grave, will be unclean for seven days.

verses.text: “Go away! Unclean!” men shouted at them. “Away, away! Do not touch us!” So they fled and wandered. Among the nations it was said, “They can stay here no longer.”

xrefs.text: A diseased person must wear torn clothes and let his hair hang loose, and he must cover his mouth and cry out, ‘Unclean, unclean!’

verses.text: The presence of the LORD has scattered them; He regards them no more. The priests are shown no honor; the elders find no favor.

xrefs.text: Princes have been hung up by their hands; elders receive no respect.
So the LORD will cut off Israel’s head and tail, both palm branch and reed in a single day.
I would have said that I would cut them to pieces and blot out their memory from mankind,

It will not be like the covenant I made with their fathers when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, because they did not abide by My covenant, and I disregarded them, declares the Lord.
I will make them a horror and an offense to all the kingdoms of the earth, a disgrace and an object of scorn, ridicule, and cursing wherever I have banished them.

verses.text: All the while our eyes were failing as we looked in vain for help. We watched from our towers for a nation that could not save us.

xrefs.text: Egypt will never again be an object of trust for the house of Israel, but will remind them of their iniquity in turning to the Egyptians. Then they will know that I am the Lord GOD.”

Those who made Cush their hope and Egypt their boast will be dismayed and ashamed.

I called out to my lovers, but they have betrayed me. My priests and elders perished in the city while they searched for food to keep themselves alive.

verses.text: They stalked our every step, so that we could not walk in our streets. Our end drew near, our time ran out, for our end had come!

xrefs.text: “Amos, what do you see?” He asked. “A basket of summer fruit,” I replied. So the LORD said to me, “The end has come for My people Israel; I will no longer spare them.”
“O son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says to the land of Israel: ‘The end! The end has come upon the four corners of the land.
May no slanderer be established in the land; may calamity hunt down the man of violence.

But for now I will send for many fishermen, declares the LORD, and they will catch them. After that I will send for many hunters, and they will hunt them down on every mountain and hill, even from the clefts of the rocks.
Without cause my enemies hunted me like a bird.

verses.text: Those who chased us were swifter than the eagles in the sky; they pursued us over the mountains and ambushed us in the wilderness.

xrefs.text: Their horses are swifter than leopards, fiercer than wolves of the night. Their horsemen charge ahead, and their cavalry comes from afar. They fly like a vulture, swooping down to devour.
Behold, he advances like the clouds, his chariots like the whirlwind. His horses are swifter than eagles. Woe to us, for we are ruined!
He lifts a banner for the distant nations and whistles for those at the ends of the earth. Behold— how speedily and swiftly they come!
“No,” you say, “we will flee on horses.” Therefore you will flee! “We will ride swift horses,” but your pursuers will be faster.
The LORD will bring a nation from afar, from the ends of the earth, to swoop down upon you like an eagle— a nation whose language you will not understand,

verses.text: The LORD’s anointed, the breath of our life, was captured in their pits. We had said of him, “Under his shadow we will live among the nations.”

xrefs.text: But I will spread My net over him, and he will be caught in My snare. I will bring him to Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans; yet he will not see it, and there he will die.

But the army of the Chaldeans pursued them and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. They seized him and brought him up to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he pronounced judgment on him.
But Abishai son of Zeruiah said, “Shouldn’t Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the LORD’s anointed?”
Then the LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living being.
So David asked him, “Why were you not afraid to lift your hand to destroy the LORD’s anointed?”

verses.text: So rejoice and be glad, O Daughter of Edom, you who dwell in the land of Uz. Yet the cup will pass to you as well; you will get drunk and expose yourself.

There was a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job. And this man was blameless and upright, fearing God and shunning evil.
Remember, O LORD, the sons of Edom on the day Jerusalem fell: “Destroy it,” they said, “tear it down to its foundations!”
For the LORD humbled Judah because Ahaz king of Israel had thrown off restraint in Judah and had been most unfaithful to the LORD.

Remember, O LORD, the sons of Edom on the day Jerusalem fell: “Destroy it,” they said, “tear it down to its foundations!”

In those days and at that time, declares the LORD, a search will be made for Israel’s guilt, but there will be none, and for Judah’s sins, but they will not be found; for I will forgive the remnant I preserve.
So rejoice and be glad, O Daughter of Edom, you who dwell in the land of Uz. Yet the cup will pass to you as well; you will get drunk and expose yourself.
